diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $(X,|\cdot|_X),(Y,|\cdot|_Y)$ be  Banach spaces  with the Approximation Property, i.e. we are given $\left\{{\mathcal S}^X_\alpha\right\}_{\alpha \in A }\subset \mathcal L(X)$, $\left\{{\mathcal S}^Y_\beta\right\}_{\beta \in B }\subset \mathcal L(Y)$ satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:approx_pro}.
Since ${\mathcal S}^Y_\beta\xrightarrow{co} I$ (recall Assumption \ref{ass:approx_pro}), we can find $\beta \in B$ such that $I_{1}^{\beta,i}<\epsilon/3$.

issues.failure_explanation: The contributions paragraph asserts that Theorem th:UAT_K_Banach achieves UA in $C_B^k(X;Y)^{co}$ 'via EDAs under only AP on $X$'. The theorem is stated and proved under the Approximation Property of both spaces: the Section 4.2 setup explicitly provides nets $\{\mathcal S^X_\alpha\}\subset\mathcal L(X)$ and $\{\mathcal S^Y_\beta\}\subset\mathcal L(Y)$ satisfying Assumption ass:approx_pro, and the proof's term $I_1^{\beta,i}=\sup_{y\in Z_K}|(I-\mathcal S^Y_\beta)y|$ is made small using $\mathcal S^Y_\beta\xrightarrow{co}I$ on $Y$, i.e. AP of $Y$, which is essential for reconstructing the $Y$-valued outputs through a fixed finite-dimensional decoder. The paper nowhere establishes the theorem without AP on $Y$. The prose thus claims the UAT under a strictly weaker hypothesis than what is assumed and used.

failure_location.quote: via EDAs under only AP on $X$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the prose to 'under AP on $X$ and $Y$' (or supply a proof that AP on $Y$ can be dropped, which the source does not contain).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised hypothesis strength of the main compact-open UAT is misstated: a reader is led to believe AP on the output space $Y$ is unnecessary. No formal result is invalidated; Theorem th:UAT_K_Banach itself is correctly stated relative to its Section 4.2 setup.
issues.title: Introduction claims the compact-open UAT holds 'under only AP on X', but Theorem th:UAT_K_Banach requires the Approximation Property on both X and Y
issues.why_classification: A one-line local prose correction restores consistency between the introduction and the theorem; every theorem, proof, rate, and advertised guarantee in the paper is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that the space depends on $\left\{{\mathcal S}^X_d\right\}_{d\in \mathbb N }$, $\left\{{\mathcal S}^Y_m\right\}_{m \in \mathbb N}$, even if not emphasized in the notation.
Moreover, taking ${\mathcal E}^X=I$ (on $X$), ${\mathcal D}^Y=I$ (on $Y$) all spaces trivially collapse in the finite-dimensional case, proving \eqref{eq:CkBmuc(X,Y)=Ckw-eq}.

issues.failure_explanation: In the claimed equality chain, the CC-space is defined relative to prescribed BAP sequences (canonically the ONB projections, per Definition def:orthonormal_basis) and requires $\|f^{N_d,N_m}\|_{\mathcal W^{k,p}_{\mu^{0,\mathcal E^X_d}}}<\infty$ for ALL $d,m$. In Prop (ii) no growth condition on $F\in C^{k;p}_{\mu_0}$ and no moment condition on the arbitrary finite measure $\mu^0$ is assumed, so this finiteness is not automatic and fails in general. Counterexample: $X=Y=\mathbb R^2$, canonical projection sequences, $\mu^0=\sum_n 2^{-n}\delta_{(n,n^2)}$, $\eta$ a Gaussian on $(\mathbb R^2)^k$, and $F\in C^\infty$ vanishing near the atoms $(n,n^2)$ with $F(n,0)=(2^n,0)$. Then $\|F\|_{\mathcal W^{k,p}_{\mu^0}}=0$, so $F$ lies in the other four spaces (e.g. in the Cyl/A-spaces via the trivial encoder $\mathcal E=I$), but for $d=1$, $\int|F(y,0)|^p\,d((\mathcal E^X_1)_#\mu^0)(y)=\sum_n 2^{-n}2^{np}=\infty$, so $F\notin C^{k;p}_{B,\mu,CC}$. The proof's step 'taking $\mathcal E^X=I$ ... all spaces trivially collapse' is an invalid inference for the CC-space: the freedom to choose the identity encoder exists for the Cyl/A-spaces but not for the CC-space, which is bound to the pre-specified sequences; moreover, the proposition never specifies which BAP sequences the CC-space refers to, so the equality is also ill-defined as stated. (The same finiteness condition is proved in Theorem th:relations_sobolve_norms (v) only under growth and moment hypotheses, confirming it is not automatic.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the equality without the $C^{k;p}_{B,\mu,CC}$ term (the other four spaces do coincide in finite dimensions), or specify that in finite dimensions the BAP sequences are chosen trivially ($\mathcal S_d\equiv I$), or add the growth/moment hypotheses under which the CC-conditions are verified (as done in Theorem th:relations_sobolve_norms (v)).
issues.overall_effect: The CC-link of \eqref{eq:CkBmuc(X,Y)=Ckw-eq} is unreliable (false under the canonical instantiation of the BAP sequences, ill-defined without specifying them). The finite-dimensional consistency of the remaining four spaces, and all other results in the paper (none of which use this CC-link; the Hornik-recovery remark uses only the four-space collapse) are unaffected.
issues.title: Finite-dimensional 'collapse' equality in Prop. prop:relations_sobolev_norms_1 falsely includes the sequence-dependent CC-space
issues.why_classification: A short, local repair (deleting one term from the equality chain, or specifying the approximating sequences) fixes the proposition; no downstream labelled result relies on the CC-link, and the substantive finite-dimensional consistency claim survives via the other four spaces.
